finding_dispositions.note: Hom. 11 was re-read whole in the tracked NPNF1 13 text (54274dd9 matched). The gloss and the no-inferiority sentence are quoted without the ellipsis in scope 3.3 and interpretations 2.2, with the practical point on vv. 4-6 ('called on the same terms', 'a greater God, another, of a lesser God', 'whence is it that ye are high-minded?'). The Greek was read on IA page image PG 62 leaf n83, col. 80 (efd4c7cd...). It glosses the first phrase as 'who is above all' with no word for NPNF's 'the Lord'. The glosses on 'through all' (pronoon, dioikon) and 'in all' (oikon) share their roots with Theodoret's pronoia and enoikesis; the record says so, and it says Theodoret's 'lordship' matches the English 'the Lord', not Migne. Theodoret's vv. 5-6 were re-read on leaf n289 (digest matched), including the concord sentence. Aquinas lect. 2 on 4:6 was read on the registered Dessain facsimile (pp. 316-317). He first commends the one God's dignity 'ex tribus' and only then appropriates, and scope 4.5 records that he holds both lines. Chrysostom's 'this' does not name the phrase. The record gives 'through all' as its own inference, with its basis, and does not attribute it to Chrysostom. Scope 3.3 (Greek, Medieval and Retained-use rows), 4.5, 5.2 and 6.2 were rewritten, as were interpretations 1.2, 1.6, 2.1, 2.2, 2.5 and 2.6. The NPNF binding's context was updated.

notes: Records written, all inside the leaf: research/scope.md, research/interpretations.md, research/source-bindings.toml and research/review-dependencies.toml. Nothing was committed and no shared file was edited. The new bindings, found by tools/source-library fingerprint, are the Dessain facsimile (book-facsimile-e8b81493) and the Parma vol. 14 OCR. The Dessain OCR binding gained two loci. The psalm-concordance binding context was corrected, because the traced chronology run does not open that concordance. Checks: source-library validate passes, the research-preflight gate command (_proper_study.py check --phase research) passes, proper-chronology record and annotations --check are current, and the research seal command runs. Every src/sources file the traced computation opens falls under a declared path. RES-016 (advisory): a Medieval-and-later row was added to scope 3.7. It records Aquinas, Super Phil. c. 4 on 4:6, citing Dan 9:18, read on the Dessain facsimile p. 398. It also records the negative: no Daniel commentary by a Doctor or canonized exegete is held (candidate authors' holdings listed; the Parma vol. 14 dissertation rejects the pseudo-Thomist Daniel), and a literal search of all tracked texts for the wording of Dan 9:17-19. Scope 5.2 names the family as unreached, with St Albert the Great first. RES-017 (advisory): the book-index artifact, the Clementine chapters directory, and the Douay, RV and WEB-C edition directories are declared in review-dependencies.toml, and scope 7.5 is rewritten; the trace was re-run independently. Report to the workflow owner: the engine's v3 seal (CHRONOLOGY_COMPUTATION_INPUTS, code only) and its docstring agree that corpus and concordance data are research's to declare, and propers-three-documents.md says the same. What no guidance or tool states is which data files the computation opens. Each leaf therefore has to find them with an audit-hook trace, and a missed one goes unsealed. Recommended fix: have the engine seal those data inputs with the code, or emit their list. Remaining limitations: the Greek base of the NPNF Ephesians translation is unidentified; Chrysostom's Greek was read only at col. 80; the PG 62 and n289 page images are unregistered; the Parma dissertation and the Super Gal. Dan 9:27 citation are optical-layer only; the literal Daniel search cannot catch damaged OCR or paraphrase; and the earlier limits in scope 5.2 and 10 stand.
summary: Research's third reentry for the Claude leaf 57-seventeenth-after-pentecost repaired RES-015. Chrysostom's hom. 11 gloss on Eph 4:6 is now quoted whole from the tracked NPNF1 13 text and was read in the Greek on the Migne PG 62 col. 80 page image. Scope section 4.5 now gives two lines of exegesis: Jerome distributes and Aquinas appropriates the phrases to the three Persons, and Chrysostom and Theodoret read them as three relations of the one God and Father. Chrysostom adds the no-inferiority argument and Theodoret draws concord; every 'third reading/mechanism/sense' is removed. The work also cleared advisories RES-016 (the Offertory's medieval-and-later row and its negative result) and RES-017 (the canon and concordance data the chronology computation reads, now declared).
